comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the allosteric activation mechanism (C50-C58). OpenEval emphasizes the converging evidence from size exclusion chromatography and kinase assays with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this finding as 'convincing' with all three reviewers supporting the allosteric activation conclusion.

Perfect agreement on claims C63-C100 regarding Y836F and SSAA mutations blocking receptor complex activation. Both evaluations find the data convincing. OpenEval highlights the complementary assays and consistent impairment across readouts. Peer reviewers specifically praise the 'clear 32P-based biochemistry' as foundational evidence.

Strong agreement on HDX-MS data (C67-C73). OpenEval confirms the data meet consensus guidelines with appropriate statistical analysis and structural interpretation. Peer reviewers 'particularly liked' the HDX experiments, describing them as providing 'novel mechanistic insights' and part of a 'convincing set' of evidence.

Both evaluations strongly support the functional rescue data (C74-C85, C92-C93). OpenEval emphasizes the multiple independent assays across expression systems with appropriate statistics. Peer reviewers specifically praise 'the design and testing of the kinase activating mutations' as providing novel insights with 'logical and well-controlled approaches.'

Divergent evaluations of claims C101-C103. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to inconsistent replicates (restoration in only 2 of 4 experiments) and calls for additional data. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting this as part of the overall convincing biochemical evidence without noting the variability concerns.

Perfect agreement on reciprocal rescue experiments (C105-C112). Both evaluations find the data strongly support the allosteric activation model. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental design testing alternative mechanisms. Peer reviewers describe the approach as 'logical and well-controlled' with 'clear and convincing' data.

Strong agreement on XIIa family member analysis (C117-C130). OpenEval notes systematic testing with appropriate controls while acknowledging interpretation limitations. Peer reviewers view this as 'nicely extended' work providing 'an explanation of why so many Arabidopsis kinases are pseudokinases' and evidence for broader conservation.

Perfect agreement on the central mechanistic model (C10-C11, C131-C133, C138-C139, C141). Both evaluations strongly support the αC-helix stabilization mechanism. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers describe it as 'convincing' and representing 'a significant advancement' providing 'a new paradigm.'

Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the sequential phosphorylation model as consistent with the data without noting the lack of direct temporal evidence.
